items.title: Full saved overview — Indonesia
kv: Indonesia now has a measurable OJK-supervised crypto stack: two exchanges, two clearing/guarantee/settlement institutions, two custodians and 27 licensed dealers at the August supervisory cutoff, serving 22.93 million accounts and IDR 20.52 trillion of July spot transactions. PT Adhyoka Berkah Maju's IDRP rupiah-stablecoin business model passed the OJK sandbox on 11 June, but no reviewed record establishes an issuer licence, public launch, reserves, redemption or lawful payment use. Bank Indonesia still separates crypto trading from legal rupiah payment, while Bank Mandiri, BRI, BNI, BCA and other banks scale conventional QRIS/account-money corridors. Digital Rupiah remains an experimental future central-bank claim, not production money.

items.title: Authority
kv: OJK took crypto and digital-financial-asset supervision from Bappebti on 10 January 2025 and now licenses exchanges, clearing/guarantee/settlement institutions, custodians and dealers under POJK 27/2024 as amended by POJK 23/2025. Bank Indonesia retains currency, payment-system, FX, QRIS, BI-FAST/RTGS and Digital Rupiah authority; PPATK and enforcement bodies retain AML and crime-response functions.
OJK trading or sandbox authority does not authorize a payment instrument or central-bank liability; BI payment authority does not license a crypto dealer.

items.title: Legal objects
kv: The regime separates traded digital financial assets and cryptoassets, digital-asset derivatives, dealer cash entitlements, segregated commercial-bank deposits, custodied cryptoassets, a sandbox-tested rupiah stablecoin model, bank/e-money rupiah balances and experimental Digital Rupiah. BI says Digital Rupiah would be a direct central-bank claim and is neither crypto nor stablecoin.
A QR credential, bank deposit, cryptoasset, sandbox stablecoin and CBDC are different legal objects; reference to rupiah does not make a private token legal tender.

items.title: Permitted activities
kv: Licensed entities operate crypto exchanges, clearing/guarantee/settlement, storage and dealer trading, including listed derivatives within their scope. Payment providers process rupiah account and QR payments. Stablecoin issuance has a passed sandbox model but no retrieved issuer licence; virtual-currency payment processing remains prohibited. Staking, lending and each tokenized-asset permission still require activity-specific confirmation.
Exchange listing, sandbox passage, dealer licence, custody, derivatives trading and payment use are separate permissions.

items.title: Entry gates
kv: OJK licensing applies separately to exchanges, clearing/settlement institutions, custodians and dealers; each exchange controls its Digital Financial Asset List. PADK 3/2026 supplies current reporting procedures. Similar business models may seek registration after a sandbox model passes, but passage is not registration. Segregated consumer accounts may be opened only at an OJK-licensed commercial bank.
Sandbox, registration, licence, list admission, bank-account access and payment-provider admission are different gates.

items.title: Named operating actors
kv: Named crypto actors include exchanges CFX and ICEX, licensed dealer PT Indonesia Digital Exchange, denied applicant PT Gerbang Aset Digital and sandbox participant PT Adhyoka Berkah Maju/IDRP. Major payment banks include Bank Mandiri, BRI, BNI, BCA and BSI. The public aggregate confirms two clearing institutions and two custodians but the normalized card still requires a current exact-name roster for every entity.
A bank/PJP role in rupiah payments or segregated accounts does not establish crypto issuance or custody; a sandbox participant is not automatically licensed.

items.title: Claims and backing
kv: Rupiah bank and e-money balances remain claims on their exact providers; segregated crypto customer funds sit as commercial-bank deposits under the market arrangement; cryptoasset ownership and custody run through dealer/custodian records; future Digital Rupiah would be a BI claim. IDRP's reserve owner, eligible assets, bank, attestation, redemption and insolvency terms were not established by the sandbox result.
Segregated bank money does not guarantee a crypto price or private stablecoin; sandbox success is not reserve or redemption evidence.

kv: BI-RTGS, BI-FAST, QRIS and regulated bank/e-money providers supply production money. Crypto trading adds exchange, clearing/guarantee/settlement, custody, dealer and segregated-bank-account records. BCA's September notice and BRI's merchant materials show that merchant payout can occur in batches after customer confirmation. Project Garuda remains experimental.
Customer QR confirmation, dealer ledger, chain transfer, merchant payout, clearing obligation and final central-bank-money transfer can occur on different clocks.

items.title: Cross border routes
kv: QRIS and local-currency arrangements connect Indonesia with named regional partners. The Indonesia-to-Japan route is live: an Indonesian user authorizes a domestic account debit, FX and switching occur through corridor actors, and the Japanese merchant receives yen. Nexus membership and BI-FAST connection remained under development for a targeted 2027 go-live.
Production fiat-account connectivity is not a stablecoin, crypto or CBDC corridor, and interface confirmation is not the final institutional settlement record.

kv: July spot value fell 28.20 percent and derivatives value 18.53 percent month over month while accounts increased. Satgas PASTI stopped 228 illegal dealers through May, and OJK issued three written warnings to two unnamed operators in August. No licensed exchange default, custodian shortfall, IDRP depeg/redemption failure or Digital Rupiah incident was located.
Lower volume, illegal activity, a warning, insolvency, customer-asset shortfall and settlement failure are different stress states.

items.title: Correction and loss
kv: After denying PT Gerbang Aset Digital's dealer application, OJK cancelled its inherited candidate status and required clear settlement of customer rights and obligations plus a complaint channel. Market rules allocate records across dealer, exchange, clearing and custodian, but no observed licensed-provider failure exposes the full waterfall. QR payout and user-error rules remain bank and route specific.
Regulatory exit obligations do not prove every customer has been repaid; bank transfer error, crypto custody loss and clearing default require different correction routes.

authority.summary: OJK took crypto and digital-financial-asset supervision from Bappebti on 10 January 2025 and now licenses exchanges, clearing/guarantee/settlement institutions, custodians and dealers under POJK 27/2024 as amended by POJK 23/2025. Bank Indonesia retains currency, payment-system, FX, QRIS, BI-FAST/RTGS and Digital Rupiah authority; PPATK and enforcement bodies retain AML and crime-response functions.
authority.boundary: OJK trading or sandbox authority does not authorize a payment instrument or central-bank liability; BI payment authority does not license a crypto dealer.

legal_objects.summary: The regime separates traded digital financial assets and cryptoassets, digital-asset derivatives, dealer cash entitlements, segregated commercial-bank deposits, custodied cryptoassets, a sandbox-tested rupiah stablecoin model, bank/e-money rupiah balances and experimental Digital Rupiah. BI says Digital Rupiah would be a direct central-bank claim and is neither crypto nor stablecoin.
legal_objects.boundary: A QR credential, bank deposit, cryptoasset, sandbox stablecoin and CBDC are different legal objects; reference to rupiah does not make a private token legal tender.

permitted_activities.summary: Licensed entities operate crypto exchanges, clearing/guarantee/settlement, storage and dealer trading, including listed derivatives within their scope. Payment providers process rupiah account and QR payments. Stablecoin issuance has a passed sandbox model but no retrieved issuer licence; virtual-currency payment processing remains prohibited. Staking, lending and each tokenized-asset permission still require activity-specific confirmation.
permitted_activities.boundary: Exchange listing, sandbox passage, dealer licence, custody, derivatives trading and payment use are separate permissions.

entry_gates.summary: OJK licensing applies separately to exchanges, clearing/settlement institutions, custodians and dealers; each exchange controls its Digital Financial Asset List. PADK 3/2026 supplies current reporting procedures. Similar business models may seek registration after a sandbox model passes, but passage is not registration. Segregated consumer accounts may be opened only at an OJK-licensed commercial bank.
entry_gates.boundary: Sandbox, registration, licence, list admission, bank-account access and payment-provider admission are different gates.

named_operating_actors.summary: Named crypto actors include exchanges CFX and ICEX, licensed dealer PT Indonesia Digital Exchange, denied applicant PT Gerbang Aset Digital and sandbox participant PT Adhyoka Berkah Maju/IDRP. Major payment banks include Bank Mandiri, BRI, BNI, BCA and BSI. The public aggregate confirms two clearing institutions and two custodians but the normalized card still requires a current exact-name roster for every entity.
named_operating_actors.boundary: A bank/PJP role in rupiah payments or segregated accounts does not establish crypto issuance or custody; a sandbox participant is not automatically licensed.

claims_and_backing.summary: Rupiah bank and e-money balances remain claims on their exact providers; segregated crypto customer funds sit as commercial-bank deposits under the market arrangement; cryptoasset ownership and custody run through dealer/custodian records; future Digital Rupiah would be a BI claim. IDRP's reserve owner, eligible assets, bank, attestation, redemption and insolvency terms were not established by the sandbox result.
claims_and_backing.boundary: Segregated bank money does not guarantee a crypto price or private stablecoin; sandbox success is not reserve or redemption evidence.

domestic_rails.summary: BI-RTGS, BI-FAST, QRIS and regulated bank/e-money providers supply production money. Crypto trading adds exchange, clearing/guarantee/settlement, custody, dealer and segregated-bank-account records. BCA's September notice and BRI's merchant materials show that merchant payout can occur in batches after customer confirmation. Project Garuda remains experimental.
domestic_rails.boundary: Customer QR confirmation, dealer ledger, chain transfer, merchant payout, clearing obligation and final central-bank-money transfer can occur on different clocks.

cross_border_routes.summary: QRIS and local-currency arrangements connect Indonesia with named regional partners. The Indonesia-to-Japan route is live: an Indonesian user authorizes a domestic account debit, FX and switching occur through corridor actors, and the Japanese merchant receives yen. Nexus membership and BI-FAST connection remained under development for a targeted 2027 go-live.
cross_border_routes.boundary: Production fiat-account connectivity is not a stablecoin, crypto or CBDC corridor, and interface confirmation is not the final institutional settlement record.

operating_state.summary: QRIS/LCT corridors were in production at bounded scopes; the Indonesia-Japan direction was live; Nexus was in implementation; and Digital Rupiah was experimental with no production issuance located.
operating_state.boundary: Production corridor, membership, development, proof of concept and production currency issuance are different states.

scale.summary: OJK reported 22.93 million dealer customer accounts in July, up 1.03 percent monthly; IDR 20.52 trillion spot crypto value, down 28.20 percent; and IDR 3.41 trillion derivatives value, down 18.53 percent. CFX listed 1,214 assets and 49 derivatives and ICEX 871 assets. BCA cited 7.6 million cross-border QRIS transactions since the start of 2026; major banks also disclose bank-specific QR value.
scale.boundary: Accounts are not unique active persons; exchange lists can overlap; transaction value is not net flow, holdings, reserves or bank settlement exposure.

stress.summary: July spot value fell 28.20 percent and derivatives value 18.53 percent month over month while accounts increased. Satgas PASTI stopped 228 illegal dealers through May, and OJK issued three written warnings to two unnamed operators in August. No licensed exchange default, custodian shortfall, IDRP depeg/redemption failure or Digital Rupiah incident was located.
stress.boundary: Lower volume, illegal activity, a warning, insolvency, customer-asset shortfall and settlement failure are different stress states.

correction_and_loss.summary: After denying PT Gerbang Aset Digital's dealer application, OJK cancelled its inherited candidate status and required clear settlement of customer rights and obligations plus a complaint channel. Market rules allocate records across dealer, exchange, clearing and custodian, but no observed licensed-provider failure exposes the full waterfall. QR payout and user-error rules remain bank and route specific.
correction_and_loss.boundary: Regulatory exit obligations do not prove every customer has been repaid; bank transfer error, crypto custody loss and clearing default require different correction routes.

evidence_boundary.summary: The country now has an official legal, licence and aggregate-scale baseline through the August supervisory release. The latest public monthly market values cover July, provider shares and balances are not public, the IDRP result is sandbox-only, and FEKDI policy statements add no issuer licence or production CBDC receipt.
evidence_boundary.boundary: Official aggregates do not establish private reserve records, confidential incident reports, beneficial ownership, or later legal and market developments.

uncertain: This is the country record at its saved cutoff, not a current-status refresh.
Research coverage states do not measure adoption. Each instrument, permission and operating claim keeps its own evidence.

catalog_context.title: Crypto around the world: many licenses, no proven cross-border use
catalog_context.answer: Across 22 jurisdictions, we found no verified cross-border payment route that depends on crypto from end to end. The token layer still settles through ordinary banks and national payment systems.
